messages:
alex.k: Ran the scheduled night experiment to reduce PD noise (23:00-03:00 window). TL;DR: we enabled a temporary hold that groups low-severity alerts into a digest and rate-limited repeat fingerprints. Results attached below.

mira_ops: Nice — did we hit any missed customer-impacting alerts while the hold was active?

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2032-678 (automated grouping digest) — alerts were buffered and posted to #eng-sre-nightly-digests.

jordan_sre: No customer-facing incidents reported from SRE oncall or support during the window. We correlated PD pages with Support tickets and saw no escalation.

lee_platform: I pulled metric comparisons. Key numbers: total PD pages down 78% overnight, unique alert fingerprints down 65%, but normalization ratio (true-positive/alerts) improved by ~30%.

alex.k: Prometheus query I used to measure repeaters (feel free to reuse):
```promql
sum by(alertname, fingerprint)(increase(alertmanager_alerts_total[4h]))
```

mira_ops: What about detection lag? Were any high-priority alerts delayed because they matched the hold rule?

jordan_sre: We had one medium-priority CPU spike alert that matched the fingerprint policy and was held for 7m before digesting. Oncall noticed via the digest and escalated. Impact: negligible. We should tighten the rule to exempt alerts with severity=critical or alerts that cross a runbook threshold.

alex.k: Agreed. The temp rule was intentionally permissive to gather signals — not a long-term config. Current plan: exempt labels {severity=~"critical|sev0|sev1"} and alerts whose runbook contains 'service:api' from the hold.

lee_platform: For rollout I also recommend adding a short-circuit: if post-buffer rate for a fingerprint exceeds X pages/minute then immediately promote to PD. Otherwise digest. Example pseudo-config we tested:
```yaml
- matchers:
  - severity: low
  - fingerprint_repeats: ">=3"
  action: buffer_digest
  immediate_escalate_if: "repeat_rate > 1/min"
```

mira_ops: We should also add dashboards so oncall can see 'buffer size' and 'time-to-first-digest' in real-time. I made a quick Grafana panel and shared a link in #eng-sre-private.

alert-audit-bot: Audit: PD events suppressed between 23:01 and 02:59: 163 events buffered, 41 unique fingerprints ingested.

jordan_sre: Follow-ups I propose: 1) Add severity exemptions in the hold rule (PR), 2) Instrument buffer latency metric (prometheus), 3) Create a PD runbook snippet for 'digest-notes' so oncall knows how to treat grouped alerts.

alex.k: I'll open PRs for 1 and 2 today. Also scheduling a short async review with Platform to validate 'immediate_escalate_if' thresholds.

lee_platform: One caveat: we saw a false negative on a noisy synthetic check that was actually a client-side regression; digesting made it less visible until morning. To prevent that, we should exclude 'synthetic/checks/*' alerts or route them to a separate non-buffered channel.

mira_ops: Good catch. Add to the exceptions list. Also recommend a gradual rollout: enable buffering only 00:00-04:00 for the next two weeks and monitor.

alex.k: Postmortem note draft: 'Nightly PD squelch experiment reduced wakeups by ~78% with no observed customer escalations. Two tuning items: exclude synthetic checks and ensure severity-runbook exemptions. Post-rollout, create metric alerts for buffer overrun and digest lag.'

jordan_sre: I'll prepare the digest template and include a quick 'action card' for each buffered fingerprint: observed count, top 3 affected hosts, last-sample logs. That made triage much faster during the run.

lee_platform: One more ops improvement: add a lightweight automated smoke script that runs when buffer > 50 and asserts critical endpoints. If smoke fails, auto-promote the digest to PD.

mira_ops: Sounds good. Can we also add an annotation to PD incidents created from digest promotion so we can slice postmortem data by 'promoted_from_digest=true'?

alex.k: Yep — will add that to the PR.

jordan_sre: Action items in one list (quick):
- alex.k: PR for hold rule + exemptions (due EOD)
- alex.k: PR to add buffer latency metric (due EOD)
- lee_platform: add immediate_escalate_if logic to runtime (due +2 days)
- jordan_sre: digest template + runbook snippet (due +1 day)
- mira_ops: dashboard panels + alerting for buffer overrun (due +2 days)
- all: gradual nightly rollout 00:00-04:00 for 2 weeks, then reassess

oncall-bot: Reminder set: review experiment metrics in 14 days. :alarm_clock:

alex.k: Thanks everyone — overall happy with the signal we got. Will post a short writeup in /docs/incident-playbooks when PRs merge. :thumbsup:
